The suspects arrested over the production of counterfeit footwear at a factory in Makun, Sagamu, Ogun State, have admitted that using imitated foreign brand names helped the company attract more customers and record higher sales than products marketed under Nigerian-made branding. The Police Special Fraud Unit, Lagos, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday, following an investigation into the activities of Meibalun International Nigeria Limited, which allegedly produced and marketed footwear bearing the trademarks of international brands without authorisation. The suspects were identified as Ojeleye Esther, Olulenu Adebola, Adewunmi Titilayo and two Chinese nationals, Zhu Hai Chen and Zhou Hai Fen. According to the police, the company presented itself as a manufacturer of Nigerian-made footwear but was found producing shoes bearing the names and trademarks of Gucci, Nike, Timberland, Louis Vuitton, Adidas and other international brands. The statement, signed by the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Ovie Ewhubare, said further investigation by the unit’s Stock Capital Market Fraud Section also uncovered questionable financial practices within the company’s operations. He assured the public that the investigation would be conducted professionally and in accordance with due process, adding that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice.
